cohort: The study included 108 patients with pelvic floor dysfunction and 108 healthy subjects.
finding: The 3D pelvic floor ultrasound demonstrated significantly higher accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity (94.4%, 96.3%, and 92.6% respectively) compared to conventional ultrasound (80.6%, 83.3%, and 77.8% respectively) in assessing postpartum pelvic floor function.
cross-section timing: Performed after delivery, but the specific time point (e.g., weeks/months postpartum) is not mentioned.
